issue.title: Bead read model stuck at crate 0.40.0 since Oct 16: every reader rebuilds into the WAL and rolls back (~67 MB/min per parked runner)

task_type_fields.impact: Every bead read on the primary clone pays for a full replay plus a discarded SQLite rebuild instead of a cache hit. On athena on 2026-10-24, about 20 parked runners together used ~2.2 cores and ~19.7 MB/s of raw writes (15.7 MB/s cancelled, ~3.9 MB/s net to disk). They also caused per-minute WAL create/unlink churn on the root ext4 journal, during a period when processes were stuck in D state waiting on jbd2 commits under heavy swap. The TUI and any other bead reader may be hit the same way. Full write-up: athena load report (see artifact ref).
task_type_fields.location: sase-core crates/sase_core/src/bead/read_model/store.rs (rebuild / rebuild_from_replay / drop_cache_file -> invalidate_cache_in_place); cache file on athena: ~/projects/github/sase-org/sase/sase/repos/beads/.git/sase/bead-read-model/bead-read-model-e3b0c44298fc1c14.sqlite
task_type_fields.repro:
Observed on athena, 2026-10-24 ~08:10 EDT, with sase 0.18.0 and sase-core-rs 0.42.3 installed.

1. Open the primary beads clone's read model read-only (`file:...?mode=ro&immutable=1`). Its meta table still says `crate_version=0.40.0`, `frontier` timestamp `2026-10-16T14:13:36Z`, `last_refresh=rebuild` / `explicit rebuild`, generation 805, content_generation 883. The file mtime is Oct 16 10:20 EDT, but the beads repo HEAD is from Oct 24 07:35. The cache has not committed anything in 8 days.
2. Pick any parked agent runner sitting in `wait_for_dependencies` with a bead wait. Example: PID 1950974, `Waiting for agents: sase-1nn.8.4.1, sase-1nn.8.4.2 and beads: ...`. Run `strace -f -e trace=openat,close,pwrite64,write -p <pid>` for 65 s and map fds to paths. Result: 32,592 pwrite64 calls, 67.4 MB, all into `bead-read-model-<key>.sqlite-wal`. The -wal and -shm are created and unlinked every round. The main .sqlite never changes.
3. `/proc/<pid>/io` for that runner: write_bytes 21.7 GB, cancelled_write_bytes 20.75 GB. The work is written and then discarded, roughly once a minute (the 60 s wait fallback).

Expected: a crate-version mismatch rebuilds once and commits ("the next read rebuilds"), and later reads serve from the cache.

Possible mechanism (from reading store.rs only, not verified): on version mismatch, `drop_cache_file` now invalidates in place instead of unlinking. `rebuild_from_replay` then writes the snapshot under the generation CAS, loses the CAS or hits WriteFault, and ROLLBACKs. `open_and_serve` sees the version mismatch again, returns Unusable, and the caller falls back to plain replay. Nothing ever overwrites the 0.40.0 meta, so every reader repeats this.

issue.creation_reason: Found while diagnosing a load/swap spike on athena: parked agent runners rewrite the bead read model every minute and roll it back, so the cache has been frozen since Oct 16 and every reader pays for a full replay.

payload.description: Parked runners' 60 s wait fallback is where the per-minute read-model rebuild churn shows up; sase-1jy scoped that fallback
Verify links/refs/status landed after a timed-out batch

payload.entry: Verified root cause: the reproduced cache corruption is an orphaned streams_known rowid in sqlite_autoindex_meta_1 (integrity_check reports a wrong entry count while quick_check can pass), not the suspected lost-generation CAS. Statements touching streams_known then fail; earlier invalidation failures were swallowed, followed by rebuild retries that grew the WAL before rollback. The new synthetic regression reproduces this index corruption and verifies the in-place repair.

payload.description: Confirm the verified read-model corruption finding was recorded for the land agent.
Confirm the verified read-model corruption finding was recorded for the land agent.

payload.entry:
Fixed in sase-core, and both fixes are ancestors of sase's pin 800caef4:
- sase-1oh.3, 7b88b98d: rebuild() cold-rebuilds on a crate-version mismatch; the snapshot write CAS-checks generation before rewriting tables and persists the schema, reducer and crate versions; a CAS loser serves the winner only while it is fresh.
- sase-1oj.2, 651d1933: in-place repair of the verified root cause, an orphaned streams_known rowid in sqlite_autoindex_meta_1.

Regression evidence. sase-1oh.land re-ran `just test -p sase_core bead::read_model` at 800caef4: 38 passed, including the 10 tests_version convergence cases (snapshot, indexed and mutation-admission recovery; racing readers converge; a stale rebuild never overwrites a winner) and the corrupt_meta_index cases.

Live reinstall. The reinstall the plan asked for already ran through gate custom-7063d7d4-b8c2-479d-a898-66bce1310f75 (`sase update`, 2026-10-27T09:10Z). The installed sase_core_rs is 0.42.7, built from 800caef4.

Live acceptance:
- (1) passed: a read-only read of athena's primary cache meta now shows crate_version 0.42.7 with frontier 2026-10-27T11:03:47Z, where it had been stuck at 0.40.0 since 2026-10-16.
- (2) not yet met: 23 long-lived processes still map the deleted pre-update extension (parked runners from Oct 19-26, the service host, gateway, federation worker and TUI). The shared cache therefore flips crate_version among 0.42.1, 0.42.4 and 0.42.7: about 23 rebuilds per 140 s with no store change, and about 70 MB/min per stale parked runner.

That remaining churn is mixed-version fleet thrash, not this bead's stuck cache. It is recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on active epic sase-1oj (durable fix: isolate the cache per version), and sase-1oh.land raises a gate to restart the stale processes as its final action. That gate's follow-up records the gate id and the verify result here.
